name: Dr Nilofar Vazir presents papers at the International Congress for Schools Effectiveness and Improvement 2009

content.title: Dr Nilofar Vazir presents papers at the International Congress for Schools Effectiveness and Improvement 2009
content.summary: Dr Nilofar Vazir presented two papers at the International Congress for Schools Effectiveness and Improvement 2009: Departures for a learning world of quality and equality held in Vancouver, B.C, Canada from January 4-8, 2009.

media.alt: Dr Nilofar Vazir presents papers at the International Congress for Schools Effectiveness and Improvement 2009

content.text: Dr Nilofar Vazir presented two papers at the International Congress for Schools Effectiveness and Improvement 2009: Departures for a learning world of quality and equality held in Vancouver, B.C, Canada from January 4-8, 2009. Being an international forum, it provides a great opportunity for AKU-IED to disseminate its research and development work, particularly if it emanates from classroom teaching. Dr Vazir has been a member on the congress for last five years and has been invited to present papers each year. This year her paper presentation included one on 'Professional Development Portfolio as a way of transforming teachers: A case from Pakistan co-authored by Dr Vazir and Dr Ayesha Bashiruddin, Assistant Professor, AKU-IED.

The paper presented insights into a case study of six students continuous learning and transformation through professional development portfolios at AKU-IED introduced in teacher learning course. The second paper was on 'Building Capacities of Teachers in Early Childhood Education Programmes': Case studies from Pakistan co-authored by Dr Vazir and Ms Saima Khalid, Instructor, AKU-IED. The paper highlighted the effective implementation of learning from the Early Childhood Education and Development (ECED) Certificate in Education Programme offered at AKU-IED through a case study of three teachers who participated in the ECED certificate programme. The papers were received well and generated a lot of interest among the participants for further discussion and seeking insights.
